title: rdp: add dissecting of relative mouse moves
description: Last MS-RDPBCGR spec contains new messages to send relative mouse moves in fastpath packets. The patch add the dissecting of these new messages.

notes.body:
From the buildbot:
Is the mask for hf_rdp_flagsPkt correct (if so, I can disable the warning) ?


Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-rdp.c hf_rdp_flagsPkt filter= rdp.flags.pkt  - mask with non-contiguous bits SEC_PKT_MASK ( 0x4c1 )

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-rdp.c hf_rdp_fastpathRelMouseFlags_Down filter= rdp.relmouse.flags.down  - mask has odd number of digits 0x08000 expected max for FT_UINT16 is 4

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-rdp.c hf_rdp_fastpathRelMouseFlags_Down filter= rdp.relmouse.flags.down mask 0x08000 with len 5 but type FT_UINT16  indicates max of 4

> Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-rdp.c hf_rdp_flagsPkt filter= rdp.flags.pkt - mask with non-contiguous bits SEC_PKT_MASK ( 0x4c1 )

This is a long time false positive

> Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-rdp.c hf_rdp_fastpathRelMouseFlags_Down filter= rdp.relmouse.flags.down - mask has odd number of digits 0x08000 expected max for FT_UINT16 is 4
> Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-rdp.c hf_rdp_fastpathRelMouseFlags_Down filter= rdp.relmouse.flags.down mask 0x08000 with len 5 but type FT_UINT16 indicates max of 4

This one is also a false positive: 0x08000 fits on 16 bits (that's the 0 before the 8 that bothers the checker), but the checker is not smart enough to detect that. Anyway I've changed that to 0x8000 and the warning should disappear.

I have added https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13576 to avoid the false positive.

For the 2nd one, thanks, I probably care about this too much.  But if the mask's value would not fit into the 16 bits, i.e. if the extra nibble wasn't zero, it would have resulted in an error.

@alagoutte I don't understand the warning, if someone can explain why clang is unhappy...
the issue is already present on master branch, you can look https://www.wireshark.org/download/automated/analysis/scan-build-2023-12-07-100233-3112-1/report-766df6.html#EndPath for help

It's because you can call `dissect_rdp_fields(tvb, offset, pinfo, tree, authReqFields, pdu_length-6)`

Where

`rdp_field_info_t *authReqFields = NULL;`

Which means that `fields->pfield` is dereferencing a null pointer.
Or you append some things to `authReqFields` but don't append a final `rdp_field_info_t*` that has a NULL `pfield` so you run off the end of the array. Might be the latter.
Apparently in cases of unusual data in the tvb, `authReqFields` never gets set to one of the non NULL values. The base case should test for a null field.

Looks like it gets set to

`reconCookie_fields` which has three members, none of which have a NULL `pfield`, so the loop iterates three times and then runs off the end of `reconCookie_fields`
That and `passCred_fields` are not NULL terminated arrays so the array bounds check in the for loop doesn't work.
Same reason why `value_strings` end with a `{0, NULL}`
Ok fixed the terminators for these `rdp_field_info_t` arrays.
